title: What a Vending Services Program Statement Carries
content:
Where the Vending Services Program programme an agreement is written at carries client subsidy, the share of vend prices the client meets is invoiced on the statement for the period, alongside the machine lease and any one-off charges. Subsidy is the percentage of the vend price printed against the programme, held to the daily ceiling printed against the same programme for each employee on each day; a programme that carries no subsidy invoices none however the client asks.

A statement is only raised while the agreement stands active or suspended; a suspended estate is invoiced the standby charge printed against its programme for each machine in place of the lease, and no subsidy is invoiced for the suspended period. The standing of the agreement and the machines it carries are read from the vending agreement record before the statement is raised.

A service call beyond the included count printed against the programme is invoiced at the call-out charge printed against the same programme, and calls inside the included count are invoiced at nothing.

The statement is raised on the statement day printed against the programme, and a statement covering two different programmes is never raised; each agreement is stated on its own.

Where the estate's annual sales fall short of the sales the programme is written against, nothing further is invoiced, and the programme is reviewed at the next renewal instead.

### The statement read against the standing of the agreement

| Standing of the vending agreement | Statement raised | Lease or standby charge carried | Subsidy carried for the period |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Active | yes | the machine lease printed against the programme | yes, where the programme carries subsidy |
| Suspended | yes | the standby charge printed against the programme, for each machine, in place of the lease | no |
| Proposed | no | — | — |
| Closed | no | — | — |

### The subsidy figure at its ceiling (hypothetical purchases)

Subsidy is worked employee by employee and day by day. Where the share printed against the programme applied to an employee's vend prices for one day comes to less than the daily ceiling printed against that programme, the share as worked is what is invoiced for that employee on that day; where it comes to more, the ceiling is what is invoiced for that employee on that day. A programme printed as carrying no client subsidy invoices nothing under this head at all, whatever a client asks for, and the daily ceiling does not arise there.

### One statement, one agreement

A client holding vending agreements at two sites, written at two different programmes, receives a statement for each agreement on that agreement's own statement day; the two are never combined onto one statement. That each agreement is stated on its own also holds where the two agreements are written at the same programme.

### Where the year's sales fall short

The consequence the rule attaches to an estate whose annual sales fall short of the sales its programme is written against is that nothing further is invoiced on that account, and that the programme is looked at again at the next renewal. No further charge is raised on the statement for the shortfall.
